requirements.requirement: Node1 runs an enabled, persistent host firewall with the required rules surviving restart.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was active and enabled, with matching permanent and runtime rules. After node1 restarted with a different boot ID, the system returned to running state and firewalld, sshd, the SSH allowance, and all port-9000 rules were restored.

requirements.requirement: SSH to node1 is allowed from any source address.
requirements.summary: The active public zone allows the SSH service without a source restriction, and direct connections from both node2 and node3 received node1's OpenSSH banner. Node3's SSH path was also verified after restart.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is allowed only from node2 and rejected from node3 and all other sources.
requirements.summary: An ordered IPv4 rule accepts node2's address before a catch-all IPv4 reject, while a catch-all IPv6 rule rejects all IPv6 sources. Against a live listener, node2 received HTTP 200 and node3 was rejected both before and after node1's restart. The final permanent and runtime rules retained this policy.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on all three nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity consistent with the fixed lifecycle observations, recovered SSH/system state, and recovered task-path behavior.
limitations: Behavioral tests covered node2 and node3 over IPv4. The rejection of other IPv4 sources and all IPv6 sources is supported by the catch-all final firewall rules rather than exhaustive tests from additional addresses.
The lifecycle snapshots inventory services, sockets, package health, and temporary files, but do not independently capture firewalld rules; final rule state is established by executor command output.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated or unnecessary troubleshooting mutations were observed. The firewall changes were required, and the temporary port-9000 listener was removed, with the final socket inventory confirming no listener remained (cmd-2844d95df3844e22, cmd-373cfd1d996b4d6b, cmd-c20acccc4fbd4132). Hygiene is reduced because evidence probes left small temporary files: two listener logs on node1 (cmd-2844d95df3844e22, cmd-373cfd1d996b4d6b), SSH probe files on node2 (cmd-86aa413828654e92), and curl/SSH probe files on node3 (cmd-132c97f90e674b28, cmd-cc5bb5dea2694325, cmd-36679582e00f44cd, cmd-fbad0ebbf9944ef4, cmd-ced5583d99c04f03). These remained after execution rather than being cleaned. No failed services, damaged package state, or unintended listening socket was observed.
